source.title: Mid-Ulster Mail, 6 June 1964, p. 14 ("Slatequarry vacancy on Cookstown Rural Council")
source.publisher: Mid-Ulster Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: 'The other two divisions-Killeenan and Beaghmore-for which there were no nominations will again be represented by Mr. Bernard Conway and Mr. Peter Conway, respectively' (Mid-Ulster Mail, 6 June 1964, p. 14)

note: Triennial election of Cookstown Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. There were no contests for the sixteen seats. No nominations were received for Killeenan, Slatequarry and Beaghmore. Killeenan and Beaghmore 'will again be represented by Mr. Bernard Conway and Mr. Peter Conway, respectively'; Slatequarry became a casual vacancy because the retiring member, Mr. Peter Corr, did not submit his nomination paper or the subsequent form (Mid-Ulster Mail, 6 June 1964, p. 14), so it is not recorded. No nomination was received; the retiring member continued to represent the division (recorded as returned unopposed, as the earlier rounds do for no-nomination divisions). Returned unopposed.
